propositions: Operators resort to FORCE_CLOSE for ~25 administrative-disposition tickets (duplicate, obsolete, wontfix, superseded, stale-premise) where the completion verifier cannot truthfully pass them because work completion is not the intent
Non-bug tickets (task/story/epic) have no truthful administrative-disposition close path today because close_precheck.py gates the path to bugs only

The close-gate failure message does not mention or enumerate the narrowly-scoped disposition path that does exist, leaving operators with only the false choice between completing work or attesting falsely
Operators need a supported, discoverable way to close non-bug tickets with administrative classes (duplicate, obsolete, superseded, wontfix) without invoking --force
Obsolete and wontfix dispositions require a reason to justify them, and that reason must be persisted distinctly from force_close_reason and threaded through the state reducer

The close-precheck refusal message must enumerate the valid --class values applicable to each ticket type and present replacement-based (duplicate, superseded) or reason-only (obsolete, wontfix) administrative paths as truthful exits
